strings.name: Muhammad Yunus
strings.role: Economist · Grameen Bank founder · Former interim chief adviser
strings.summary: Muhammad Yunus is a Bangladeshi economist and social business advocate. His village lending experiments developed into Grameen Bank, serving borrowers without conventional collateral. He shared the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize with the bank and also faced labour-law and corruption proceedings. He led an interim government following the upheaval of 2024; his term ended in February 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected microcredit work, specific legal outcomes and the political handover through February 2026; dismissal of particular cases does not resolve every controversy.
strings.influence.rationale: He founded Grameen Bank and promoted microcredit, received the Nobel Peace Prize, and later participated in Bangladesh's transitional governance.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-1.value: Bathua village, Chittagong region, British India; now Bangladesh
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: University of Dhaka; PhD in economics, Vanderbilt University, 1969
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Grameen Bank
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Developed village lending begun in 1976 into a bank, promoting small loans for poor borrowers without conventional collateral.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Shared Nobel Peace Prize
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Shared the 2006 Peace Prize with Grameen Bank for efforts to foster economic and social development from below.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Returns to Yunus Centre
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Resumed work at the Yunus Centre after his interim government tenure, returning to social business activities.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Interim government ends
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Following elections and the new government's inauguration, a Cabinet Division notification dissolved the advisory council, ending about eighteen months of transitional rule.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Leads interim government
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Sworn in as chief adviser after Sheikh Hasina's government fell, leading the transition following student-led protests.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Acquittals in two cases
strings.timeline.event-4.text: His labour-law conviction was overturned on the 7th; he was acquitted in a separate corruption case on the 11th. These were outcomes in specific cases.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Receives Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Awarded jointly with Grameen Bank, bringing wider international attention to grassroots financial services and poverty reduction.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Grameen becomes a bank
strings.timeline.event-6.text: The earlier action research project became a formal bank, continuing lending to poor people underserved by conventional banks.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Begins village lending experiments
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Studied borrowing constraints in Jobra near Chittagong University and used small loans to help villagers reduce dependence on moneylenders.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Earns economics doctorate
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Completed his PhD at Vanderbilt, taught in the United States and returned in 1972 to join Chittagong University.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in the Chittagong region
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Born in Bathua village; later studied economics at Dhaka University before going to the United States on a Fulbright scholarship.
